sentences.cn_text: 没有哪个学科像人文学科那样热衷于专业化。
sentences.en_text: No disciplines have seized on professionalism with as much enthusiasm as the humanities.

sentences.cn_text: 正如梅南德先生所指出的，你可以在三年内成为律师，四年内成为医生。
sentences.en_text: You can, Mr. Menand points out, become a lawyer in three years and a medical doctor in four.

sentences.cn_text: 但获得人文学科博士学位的常规时间却是九年。
sentences.en_text: But the regular time it takes to get a doctoral degree in the humanities is nine years.

sentences.cn_text: 不足为奇的是，多达一半的英语博士生在获得学位前就退学了。
sentences.en_text: Not surprisingly, up to half of all doctoral students in English drop out before getting their degrees.

sentences.cn_text: 他主要关注人文学科：文学、语言、哲学等。
sentences.en_text: His concern is mainly with the humanities: literature, languages, philosophy and so on.

sentences.cn_text: 这些学科正在逐渐失宠：现在22%的美国大学毕业生主修商科，而主修历史的只有2%，主修英语的只有4%。
sentences.en_text: These are disciplines that are going out of style: 22% of American college graduates now major in business compared with only 2% in history and 4% in English.

sentences.cn_text: 然而，许多美国顶尖大学希望本科生掌握每个受过教育的人都应具备的基本经典思想。
sentences.en_text: However, many leading American universities want their undergraduates to have a grounding in the basic canon of ideas that every educated person should possess.

sentences.cn_text: 但大多数人发现很难就「通识教育」应是何种形态达成共识。
sentences.en_text: But most find it difficult to agree on what a “general education” should look like.

sentences.cn_text: 梅南德先生指出，在哈佛，「经典著作之所以被阅读，正是因为它们一直被阅读」——它们构成了某种社会粘合剂。
sentences.en_text: At Harvard, Mr. Menand notes, “the great books are read because they have been read” — they form a sort of social glue.

sentences.cn_text: 同样不足为奇的是，只有大约一半的人最终获得了他们当初进入研究生院时所期望的教授职位。
sentences.en_text: Equally unsurprisingly, only about half end up with professorships for which they entered graduate school.

sentences.cn_text: 职位实在太少了。
sentences.en_text: There are simply too few posts.

sentences.cn_text: 这部分是因为大学继续培养越来越多的博士。
sentences.en_text: This is partly because universities continue to produce ever more PhDs.

sentences.cn_text: 但愿意学习人文学科的学生却越来越少：英语系在1970-71学年授予的学士学位比20年后还要多。
sentences.en_text: But fewer students want to study humanities subjects: English departments awarded more bachelor’s degrees in 1970-71 than they did 20 years later.

sentences.cn_text: 学生减少意味着所需教师也减少。
sentences.en_text: Fewer students require fewer teachers.

sentences.cn_text: 因此，在经历十年论文写作后，许多人文学科学生离开了这个行业，去从事他们未曾接受过培训的工作。
sentences.en_text: So, at the end of a decade of thesis- writing, many humanities students leave the profession to do something for which they have not been trained.

sentences.cn_text: 设计和教授此类课程之所以困难，一个原因在于它们与美国顶尖大学的坚持相冲突——这些大学坚持将文科教育和职业教育分开，在不同学院分别教授。
sentences.en_text: One reason why it is hard to design and teach such courses is that they cut across the insistence by top American universities that liberal-arts education and professional education should be kept separate, taught in different schools.

sentences.cn_text: 许多学生同时经历这两种教育。
sentences.en_text: Many students experience both varieties.

sentences.cn_text: 尽管超过半数的哈佛本科生最终进入法律、医学或商业领域，但未来的医生和律师必须先修读非专业的文科学位，然后才能攻读职业资格。
sentences.en_text: Although more than half of Harvard undergraduates end up in law, medicine or business, future doctors and lawyers must study a non-specialist liberal-arts degree before embarking on a professional qualification.

sentences.cn_text: 除了通过这种分离使各职业专业化之外,美国顶尖大学还使教授这一职业专业化了。
sentences.en_text: Besides professionalising the professions by this separation, top American universities have professionalised the professor.

sentences.cn_text: 学术研究公共资金的增长加速了这一过程：联邦研究经费在1960年至1990年间增长了四倍，但随着研究占据更多精力，教师的教学时间减少了一半。
sentences.en_text: The growth in public money for academic research has speeded the process: federal research grants rose fourfold between 1960 and 1990, but faculty teaching hours fell by half as research took its toll.

sentences.cn_text: 专业化使获得博士学位成为成功学术生涯的先决条件：直到1969年，仍有三分之一的美国教授没有博士学位。
sentences.en_text: Professionalism has turned the acquisition of a doctoral degree into a prerequisite for a successful academic career: as late as 1969 a third of American professors did not possess one.

sentences.cn_text: 但梅南德先生认为，专业化背后的核心理念是「特定专业所需的知识和技能是可传授的，但不可迁移的」。
sentences.en_text: But the key idea behind professionalisation, argues Mr. Menand, is that “the knowledge and skills needed for a particular specialisation are transmissible but not transferable.”

sentences.cn_text: 因此，学科不仅垄断了知识的生产，也垄断了知识生产者的生产。
sentences.en_text: So disciplines acquire a monopoly not just over the production of knowledge, but also over the production of the producers of knowledge.

sentences.cn_text: 梅南德先生总结道，改革高等教育的关键是改变「知识生产者的生产方式」。
sentences.en_text: The key to reforming higher education, concludes Mr. Menand, is to alter the way in which “the producers of knowledge are produced.”

sentences.cn_text: 否则，学者们将继续危险地保持思维一致，越来越脱离他们所研究、调查和批评的社会。「学术研究，至少在某些领域，可能需要变得不那么排他，更加整体化。」
sentences.en_text: Otherwise, academics will continue to think dangerously alike, increasingly detached from the societies which they study, investigate and criticise. “Academic inquiry, at least in some fields, may need to become less exclusionary and more holistic.”

sentences.cn_text: 然而，这究竟如何实现，梅南德先生并未说明。
sentences.en_text: Yet quite how that happens, Mr. Menand does not say.

sentences.cn_text: 每一个考虑申请攻读博士学位的学生都应该阅读《思想市场：美国大学中的改革与抵制》这本精妙而睿智的小书。
sentences.en_text: The subtle and intelligent little book The Marketplace of Ideas: Reform and Resistance in the American University should be read by every student thinking of applying to take a doctoral degree.

sentences.cn_text: 读后他们可能会决定另谋出路。
sentences.en_text: They may then decide to go elsewhere.

sentences.cn_text: 因为美国大学里正在发生一些奇特的现象，而哈佛大学英语教授路易斯·梅南德巧妙地捕捉到了这一点。
sentences.en_text: For something curious has been happening in American Universities, and Louis Menand, a professor of English at Harvard University, captured it skillfully.
